name: Muhlenbergia

flags: muhlenbergia-dubia — name corrected; identification photos and native-zone range unresolved.

muhlenbergia-paniculata — Kew accepts the NAME (Muhlenbergia paniculata, synonym Schedonnardus paniculatus); existing source PHOTO species determination, fine unilateral spikelet rows and local range were not independently re-reviewed. Not a finalized visual anchor.
project_scope.note: Seven installed canonical concepts counted; M. piniflora source-concept ID and M. paniculata taxonomy/photo reviews remain flagged, not accepted as genus-key finished.

recognition.where_to_look_first: The project set spans large fountain-form bunchgrasses, small tight bunchgrasses, creeping nimblewill, and rhizomatous low muhly. Start with growth form and scale, then inspect the ligule, leaf folding/rolling, and panicle size and openness.
priority: upright bunchgrass versus creeping/rooting or rhizomatous habit
flat versus folded or involute blades
open feathery versus narrow contracted panicle
spikelet size and awn detail when the habit split is not enough

quick_split: M. lindheimeri — a LARGE coarse dense fountain clump with tall relatively contracted flower panicles and long membranous ligules.
M. reverchonii — SMALLER, more finely textured erect tuft with an airy, delicate panicle; compare true ligule and spikelet with lindheimeri.
M. schreberi — LOW weak creeping stems with short sideways leaves and narrow nearly spike-like panicle; may root from stolon nodes.
M. utilis — LOW rhizomatous grass with hair-fine inward-rolled leaves, SCALY underground rhizomes and small narrow often partly enclosed panicle.
M. paniculata (tumblegrass; formerly Schedonnardus paniculatus) — a few very LONG, slender, widely diverging one-sided racemes, often curving; look at branch shape instead of cloudlike plumes.
M. ×involuta — natural HYBRID of lindheimeri × reverchonii; intermediate stature/folded blades, but NEVER identify solely by parent-like habit.
M. piniflora — SOURCE NAME UNRESOLVED; not a taxonomically reliable field diagnosis or finished card.
comparison_lesson.nursery_warning: Do not use pink plume color by itself to call a plant M. lindheimeri. The widely sold M. capillaris concept is not a project-native Central Texas anchor.

visual_needs: PRIORITY PAIR: same-scale separately taxon-verified attached mature ligules for M. lindheimeri and M. reverchonii, measured with a millimeter ruler (published ranges partly overlap).

Nimblewill PRIORITY: actual attached stolon NODE WITH ROOTS physically photographed, short membranous ligule 10–20× with mm scale, intact very narrow mature panicle + spikelet. OSU/Penn State source study images exist; do not install third-party restricted media on public page. Emily Summerbell CC BY Commons spike and collar candidate discovered.
Genuinely exposed underground SCALY RHIZOME, rolled leaf cross-section, and small mature inflorescence for M. utilis.
Paniculata: clear TWO ROWS of spikelets on ONE SIDE of slender divergent raceme; full plant and twisted leaves.
An exact taxon-correct, reuse-permitted, verified live M. ×involuta PHOTO; existing multigrass historic plate/parent pictures do not fill this gap.
Resolve the original source concept / scientific identity of M. piniflora before visual species-ID training.
Species-level lookalike closeup of M. lindheimeri, M. reverchonii and natural hybrid ×involuta on matched scale.

Do not count photo recovery; acquire measured attached ligule and separated glumes/lemma/awn physically and verify image pixel targets. Three source-licensed wild panicle photos already ARE installed; do not solicit another general bloom.

fast_fill_note: Current learner coverage: M. schreberi 3 images; M. lindheimeri 2; M. reverchonii 1; M. utilis 1; M. ×involuta 1. M. piniflora remains excluded from fast-fill because its canonical record is scientifically PROVISIONAL and likely represents an erroneous source name. Do not pad wild-type lessons with named cultivars or uncertain-rights media.
look_here_first: MUHLY PHOTO-ID SEQUENCE — start at whole growth form: LARGE dense fountain + narrow contracted flowering heads (lindheimeri); SMALL tightly tufted hair-fine leaves + OPEN airy mature panicle (reverchonii); LOW jointed side-leaved stems (schreberi); extremely fine low patch requiring SCALY belowground rhizome (utilis); or conspicuous LONG divergent racemes (paniculata). SECOND use a fresh unfolded sheath/collar and measured membranous ligule, actual root-bearing surface node or underground rhizome where relevant, and mature spikelets. NEW three TRUE SEEP source-photographed OPEN panicles/spikelets now appear immediately after seep's fine foliage panels; dense narrow head in Lindheimer's own two photos belongs to Lindheimer. Compare open versus contracted panicle before measuring ligule. Hybrid ×involuta requires specimen-backed evidence; piniflora remains source-name HOLD. ROOTING PAIR UPDATE: nimblewill vs aparejo needs ABOVE-GROUND stolon ROOTS vs BELOW-GROUND SCALY rhizome physically demonstrated, not inferred from current foliage. Unlike nimblewill's short MEMBRANOUS ligule, bermudagrass has a fringe of hairs; check a flowerhead (nimblewill narrow contracted panicle vs Cynodon's terminal fingers).

comparison_matrix.title: Two upright muhly bunchgrasses — strongest structures
rows: Habit
Large upright stiff fountain; often ca. 0.8–1.5 m
Compact, finer, often ca. 0.4–0.8 m
Full rooted plant with ruler; sizes overlap
Leaf blades
Longer relatively coarse, 2–5 mm in many treatments
Very fine threadlike, around 1–2 mm
Fresh blade and ruler; maturity matters
Flowering head
Longer, commonly strongly contracted panicle packed with spikelets (verified head shape shown in our local photo)
Open, delicate branching mature panicle (expected botanically, not yet photographed in current source-identified seep archive)
Use the same verified flowering specimen and complete head side-on; existing Lindheimer head must NOT be treated as seep
Ligule
Usually conspicuous, long PAPERY membrane; GrassBase often 8–15 mm
Typically shorter PAPERY membrane; GrassBase 2–4(–9) mm
Open a mature attached blade–sheath junction and photograph ligule edge with mm scale; length is not completely non-overlapping
Tiny reproductive details
Usually one fertile floret; often short or absent lemma awn
One fertile floret per spikelet; one-awned lemma, short glumes (Kew: glumes generally 1–2.5[–3] mm, awn usually 0.5–3[–6] mm).
Three actual wild seep head photos resolve whole spikelets but not their component glumes/lemma/awn. Measure and dissect mature spikelets for confirmation.
Pink coloration
May vary, not reliable
Can flush reddish, not reliable
Never ID from color alone
Evidence in CURRENT local gallery
Lindheimer: dense fountainlike leaves plus narrow crowded mature inflorescence photographed; attached ligule not shown.
Seep: 2 fine foliage photos, plus 3 wild licensed OPEN inflorescence close-ups with distinct whole spikelets; attached ligule and dissected floret not shown.
Images teach whole panicle architecture and leaf habit. Same-plant measured ligule and glume/lemma/awn remains a physical macro gap.
comparison_matrix.caution: Kew GrassBase describes Lindheimer ligules 8–15 mm and seep 2–4(–9) mm, with some local treatments reporting different lengths. DO NOT impose one hard 8-mm yes/no key; match several fresh leaves, full mature inflorescence and a magnified spikelet. The existing 4-photo pair is not a same-scale matched comparison, and new three wild seep flowering photographs now illustrate an open panicle, but the ligule and separated measured floret still need same-plant photography. Hybrid ×involuta can be intermediate and must not be forced from a normal size gradient. Cultivar photos are not wild local records.

genus_field_comparison_sets.title: Large fountain vs fine small tuft
genus_field_comparison_sets.compare: MATURE PAIR PHOTO KEY: source-identified M. lindheimeri large dense stiff bunch with narrow crowded tan head versus verified wild M. reverchonii smaller threadlike tuft and TRUE OPEN ramified flowering panicle. Both are now photographically illustrated. For independent determination, verify same-plant fresh mature BLADE/SHEATH MEMBRANOUS LIGULE with mm ruler (Lindheimer commonly longer, seep usually shorter but ranges overlap) and one mature dissected glume/lemma/awn with mm scale. Never label intermediate habit as hybrid ×involuta without voucher.

genus_field_comparison_sets.title: Ground runners vs underground rhizomes
genus_field_comparison_sets.compare: At the ground, follow a WHOLE horizontal stem: nimblewill M. schreberi runs ABOVE ground with thin branching stolons that can ROOT from real lower nodes; appeared-as-a-second-species M. utilis has SCALY RHIZOMES below ground and threadlike frequently inward-rolled leaves. Existing photographs show the different foliage but NOT the rooting node or excavated rhizome. For nimblewill also find a narrow appressed spikelet-bearing panicle and a TINY MEMBRANOUS/CILIOLATE ligule. Bermuda Cynodon dactylon has fingerlike terminal racemes and a HAIR-FRINGED (not membrane) ligule. See species card for mm photo checklist; don't use sideways blades alone.

Regional scientific guides Kew, OSU, UT Extension support fine comparison.

field_key: LARGE dense fountain and narrow dense panicle: compare M. lindheimeri; verify measured collar and spikelets.
SMALL fine upright bunch and open delicate panicle: compare M. reverchonii; inspect mature spikelets and ligule at matching scale.
CREEPING above-ground jointed stems: M. schreberi; photograph a node actually rooting into soil.
LOW fine rolled leaves with SCALY underground rhizomes: M. utilis; do not call a surface runner a rhizome.
LONG divergent one-sided racemes: M. paniculata; source-photo identity remains unreviewed.
